findings.proposedIrEvidence: The rule's permission posture gives unlimited capacity to make employee/director loans/advances, subject only to a $5,000,000 outstanding cap; the only modeled conditions are the measurement-basis qualifier ('at any one time outstanding') and the key-man-insurance exception. The qualifier 'in the ordinary course of business' appears nowhere in the proposed IR.
findings.sourceEvidence: loans and advances to employees or directors of the Parent Borrower or its Subsidiaries in the ordinary course of business (including for travel, entertainment and relocation expenses) in an aggregate amount ... not to exceed $5,000,000
findings.verifierReasoning: The source's qualifying phrase 'in the ordinary course of business' is an independent, operative condition on the permission. The proposed IR's postures and conditions contain not even an UNSUPPORTED/UNQUANTIFIED representation of this qualifier. Construct a counter-example: a loan/advance to a director of $1,000,000 made outside the ordinary course of business (e.g., a one-off non-ordinary financing). Real §7.8 prohibits that advance outright (it is not within except (d)); the proposed IR would report it as permitted so long as the basket stays under $5,000,000 because nothing in the proposed IR conditions permission on ordinary-course status. That is a directly observable difference in the permission/prohibition conclusion, so the omission is material. The defect is aggravated because the IR self-certifies sufficiency as COMPLETE.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: The proposed IR models the key-man-insurance proviso as an exception (exceptionId rule[r1].exception[0]) nested under — and applicable only to — the §7.8(d) loan/advance permission rule, with description 'key man insurance is not limited by this provision'.
findings.sourceEvidence: provided, however that this provision shall not limit key man insurance;
findings.verifierReasoning: 'this provision' in the source text refers to Section 7.8, the operative clause governing all Investments (see §7.8's chapeau: 'Make any advance, loan, extension of credit ... or make any other investment in, any Person ..., except: (a)... (d)...; provided, however that this provision shall not limit key man insurance; ... (m)...'). The proviso is a standalone carve-out operating at the Section 7.8 level: it ensures key man insurance is not treated as a prohibited Investment at all, independent of whether the insurance would qualify as an employee/director loan or advance under except (d). The proposed IR instead makes it subordinate to the (d) basket, implying it only frees that basket from the cap. Construct a counter-example: key man insurance issued to a counterparty that is neither an employee nor a director of the Parent Borrower or a Subsidiary. Real §7.8 would still permit it (the proviso is a Section-level carve-out); the proposed IR would report it as prohibited because it would not fall within except (d) and the proposed IR has no exception at the Section level. That changes the permission conclusion, so this is a material logical-grouping error. (I also note the chapeau makes the operative posture under Section 7.8 a prohibition, whereas the proposed IR frames a permission exception without representing that the underlying Section-level prohibition is what gates these exceptions — but that framing is recoverable from the section citation, whereas the mis-attachment of the proviso is not.)
